newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW - Saab Auto increased Swedish sales in Sept.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Saab Auto increased Swedish sales in Sept.

text.p: Swedish carmaker Saab Automobile increased its car sales in Sweden in September, Saab Opel Sweden spokesman Torsten Aman told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday.
"Saab increased its sales in Sweden in September. I am unable to give the exact number, since the sales statistics won't become official until tonight," Aman said.
He added that Saab Automobile had a sales target of 16,500 cars in Sweden for the full year of 1996.

"That means we will not meet our 1995 Swedish sales which were 18,000 cars. On the other hand, the level of our sales today is bigger than at the same time last year, but we do not have enough time to make up for the slump at the beginning of 1996," Aman said.
Next year Saab Automobile sees sales going up even further, but Aman is reluctant to give a forecast.
"Next year we will introduce a new model which will be more expensive than the two we have today. We see a rise in sales, but by how much is difficult to say," Aman said.
In the U.S. and Great Britain, Saab Automobile is also increasing its sales. For the U.S. the full-year forecast is for 25,000-30,000 cars and for Britain 15,000 cars.
"In Britain we have already today sold more cars this year than during all of 1995. Still the U.S. is our biggest market and the market we focus most heavily on," Aman said.
